llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a legitimate Notion sync tool, but its registry metadata omits required runtime items (Node and NOTION_API_KEY) and there are mismatches between what it declares and what the included instructions and scripts actually require.
llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be a genuine Notion sync tool, but pay attention to these points before installing or running it:

- Metadata mismatch: The registry entry did not list any required environment variables or binaries, but the SKILL.md and scripts require Node.js (v18+) and a NOTION_API_KEY. Treat the NOTION_API_KEY as the primary credential and ensure Node is available where you run the scripts.

- Token sensitivity: NOTION_API_KEY is an integration token that can read/update any Notion page or database you share with the integration. Only set it if you trust the code and limit the integration's access (share only specific pages/databases when possible).

- File access: The scripts read and write local markdown files and will create/save a state file at memory/notion-watch-state.json under the current working directory. Run in a directory where you are comfortable with those files being created and where untrusted data won't be exposed.

- Verify code if you can: Because the registry metadata is inconsistent, inspect the included scripts (they are present) or run them in an isolated environment (e.g., container or sandbox) before providing your Notion token. The code in this package appears to call only api.notion.com and uses the Node https module — there are no alternate remote endpoints or obfuscated network calls in the provided source.

- Operational caution: If you allow an autonomous agent to use this skill and supply a valid token, the agent could create/update/archive pages/databases that the integration has access to. Limit the integration's permissions and shared pages to minimize blast radius.

What would increase confidence: corrected registry metadata that declares NOTION_API_KEY as a required/primary env var and Node as a required binary; or an official origin/homepage and a reproducible install/runtime guide linked from the registry entry.
